# rwgpu 0.1.0 file formats

All files are TOML. Unknown keys are errors (E0103), never ignored. Paths are relative to the project root (the folder with rwgpu.toml).

## Project: rwgpu.toml

Marks the project root. Commands find it by walking up from the given path.

### `rwgpu.toml`

Project settings. Its folder is the project root; every path in the project is relative to it.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | table: project.project | **required** | Name and entry scene. |
| `display` | table: project.display | — | Output size and background. |
| `iso` | table: project.iso | — | Isometric grid geometry. |
| `sim` | table: project.sim | — | Simulation rate and seed. |

### `[project]`

Project identity.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | Project name. |
| `engine` | string | — | rwgpu version the project targets, e.g. "0.1". `check` warns (W0205) if the running rwgpu differs. |
| `main_scene` | path | `"scenes/main.toml"` | Scene used when a command is given no scene. |

### `[display]`

The rendered frame. Screenshots and the web player use exactly this size.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | integer 1–4096 | `640` | Frame width in pixels. |
| `height` | integer 1–4096 | `480` | Frame height in pixels. |
| `background` | color | `"#1d2330"` | Color behind everything. |

### `[iso]`

Isometric projection. A cell's diamond is tile_width × tile_height pixels; one unit of height is z_height pixels.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tile_width` | integer 4–1024 | `64` | Diamond width in pixels. Usually 2 × tile_height. |
| `tile_height` | integer 2–512 | `32` | Diamond height in pixels. |
| `z_height` | integer 1–1024 | `32` | Pixels per unit of height (z, block height). |

### `[sim]`

The fixed-step simulation. A frame is one simulation step.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tick_rate` | integer 1–1000 | `60` | Steps per second. |
| `seed` | integer ≥ 0 | `1` | Seed for all randomness. Playtests and `--seed` can override it. |


## Scenes: scenes/*.toml

A scene has optional `[scene]`, `[camera]` and `[ground]` tables (with `[[terrain]]` tables for a ground `map`), then any number of `[[entity]]` and `[[connect]]` tables. Entities get ids 0, 1, 2, ... in file order (an entry with `cells` makes one entity per cell); spawned entities get the next ids.

### `scene file`

A level: ground, entities and the connections between their signals.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | table: scene.scene | — | Scene metadata. |
| `camera` | table: scene.camera | — | What part of the world is on screen. |
| `ground` | table: scene.ground | — | A rectangle of floor cells; also the bounds movers stay inside. |
| `terrain` | [[terrain]] | — | Kinds of ground used by `[ground] map`, one `[[terrain]]` table each (grass, water, ...). |
| `entity` | [[entity]] | — | Things in the world, one `[[entity]]` table each. |
| `connect` | [[connect]] | — | Signal wiring, one `[[connect]]` table each. |

### `[scene]`

Scene metadata.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | — | Display name. Default: the file name. |
| `doc` | string | — | What the scene is for. |
| `seed` | integer ≥ 0 | — | Overrides the project seed for this scene. |

### `[camera]`

Where the picture is taken from when the scene starts. The camera looks at `center` on the ground; it can turn about the vertical line through that point and zoom. A playtest's `[[input]] camera` moves it while the game runs, and however it moves, its center stays over the ground. With no keys set, the view is the isometric one of `[iso]`.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | [x, y] | — | Grid point [x, y] at the middle of the frame. Default: the middle of the ground. |
| `offset` | [x, y] | `[0, 0]` | Extra shift in screen pixels [right, down]. |
| `view` | iso \| perspective | `"iso"` | How the world is projected. `iso`: the isometric view set by `[iso]`, where parallel lines stay parallel. `perspective`: a camera 30 degrees above the horizon, where far things are drawn smaller; `center` is drawn at the same size as in `iso`. |
| `turn` | number -360–360 | `0` | Degrees the camera is turned about the vertical line through `center`. At 0, +x runs down-right and +y down-left on screen; at 90, +x runs down-left and +y up-left. |
| `zoom` | number 0.125–16 | `1.0` | Size factor: 2 draws everything in the world twice as large. Screen entities do not zoom. |

### `[ground]`

Floor cells from [0, 0] to [size_x - 1, size_y - 1], drawn as a checkerboard. Give `size` for plain ground, or `map` for ground made of terrains: one string per row (y = 0 first), one character per cell (x = 0 first), each character declared by a `[[terrain]]` table. `map = ["ggw", "gww"]` is 3 x 2 cells with water on the right.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | [x, y] int | — | Number of cells [x, y]. Required unless `map` is given (then it is the map's size). |
| `map` | ["...", ...] | — | Rows of terrain characters, all the same length: row y, character x is cell [x, y]. Every character must be declared by a `[[terrain]]` `char`. |
| `color` | color | `"#6fa86a"` | Floor color (without `map`). |
| `alt_color` | color | — | Color of every other cell. Default: `color`, slightly darker. |

### `[[terrain]]`

A kind of ground for `[ground] map`: its character, look, and whether things can be built on it. Spawned entities (`action = "spawn"`) can only be placed where every cell of their footprint is buildable.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `char` | string | **required** | The single character that marks this terrain in `[ground] map`, e.g. "g" or "~". |
| `name` | name | — | Name used in messages and `inspect`, e.g. `water`. Default: the character. |
| `color` | color | `"#6fa86a"` | Cell color. |
| `alt_color` | color | — | Color of every other cell (checkerboard). Default: `color`, slightly darker. |
| `build` | bool | `true` | Spawned entities can be placed on it. false for water, rock, roads you must keep clear. |

### `entity`

A thing in the world. Starts from an optional prefab; keys here override it (component tables merge key by key).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | name | — | Unique name, needed to reference it from [[connect]], playtests and `inspect --entity`. |
| `prefab` | name | — | Prefab to start from: `wall` loads prefabs/wall.toml. |
| `pos` | [x, y, z?] | `[0, 0, 0]` | Grid position [x, y] or [x, y, z]. +x is down-right on screen, +y is down-left, z is up. |
| `cells` | [[x, y], ...] | — | Place one copy on each listed cell instead of `pos`. Cannot be used with `name`. |
| `footprint` | [x, y] int | `[1, 1]` | Cells covered [along x, along y], from `pos` toward +x and +y: `[2, 2]` at pos [3, 4] covers [3, 4], [4, 4], [3, 5] and [4, 5]. Blocks and tiles fill the whole area; a sprite or label stands at its middle. It blocks, counts for triggers and is tapped on every covered cell. Only things that stay put can be bigger than one cell (no mover, patrol, wander, pushable or screen_pos). |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | Disabled entities are not drawn, not solid, cannot be tapped and run no behaviors. |
| `solid` | bool | `false` | Nothing can move into its cell. |
| `pushable` | bool | `false` | A crate or weight. A mover that walks into it pushes it one cell, if the cell beyond is inside the ground and free (nothing solid, no actor, no other pushable); otherwise the mover is refused (`blocked`, reason `push`). Patrols and wanderers cannot push it: it blocks them like a solid. It holds pressure plates: triggers count it like an actor (`only` can name it). It cannot have mover, patrol or wander. |
| `tile` | table: tile | — | Flat diamond on the floor (marks, pressure plates). |
| `block` | table: block | — | Isometric box (walls, crates, buildings). |
| `sprite` | table: sprite | — | Upright shape standing on the cell (characters, items). |
| `mover` | table: mover | — | Moves one cell per direction input. |
| `patrol` | table: patrol | — | Walks a fixed path of cells. |
| `wander` | table: wander | — | Walks randomly (seeded). |
| `trigger` | table: trigger | — | Emits signals when actors step on or off its cell. |
| `label` | table: label | — | Text drawn with the built-in pixel font (scores, names). |
| `screen_pos` | [x, y] | — | Draw this entity on the screen instead of in the world (a HUD): `[x, y]` is the top-left pixel of its sprite and label. Screen entities are drawn above the world, ignore the camera, can be tapped, and can only have `sprite` and `label`. |
| `props` | table | — | Game data: numbers, text and flags, e.g. `{ score = 0 }`. A prop's type is fixed by its starting value. `[[connect]]` `add`/`set` change props at runtime, `when` conditions and label `{placeholders}` read them, `inspect` shows them and `[[expect]] props` checks them. |
| `counts` | table: prop = "prefab" | — | Props that count enabled copies of a prefab, kept up to date by the engine: `counts = { houses = "house" }` makes `houses` an integer prop equal to the number of enabled `house` entities (placed in the scene or spawned; an entity with `prefab = "house"` is a copy whatever keys it overrides). It changes when a copy is spawned, disabled or enabled again; the entity then emits `changed`, so labels, `when` conditions and `[[expect]] props` read it like any prop. `add`/`set` cannot change it. |
| `allow` | ["W....", ...] | — | Warning codes that are intended for this entity and should not be reported, e.g. `["W0201"]` for deliberately stacked solids. Errors cannot be allowed. |
| `shape` | [[shape]] | — | What it is built of: solids with flat colors, one `[[shape]]` table each (in a scene: `[[entity.shape]]`, or `shape = [{ ... }]`). A list here replaces the prefab's. |

### `[[connect]]`

When `from` emits `signal`, apply `action` to `to` (or each of `actions`, in order), if every `when` condition holds. Every entity emits `tapped` when tapped; triggers emit `on_enter`/`on_exit`; an entity whose prop is changed by `add`/`set` (or whose `counts` change) emits `changed`; a spawned entity emits `spawned`; when a `spawn` cannot be placed, the source of its signal emits `refused`. `from = "ground"` listens to taps on ground cells that hit no entity (and to their refused spawns); `from_prefab` listens to every entity made from a prefab, and `to = "self"` then targets the one that emitted.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | name | — | Name of the emitting entity, or `ground` for taps on empty ground cells (signals `tapped`, and `refused` when a spawn it started cannot be placed). Use exactly one of `from` and `from_prefab`. |
| `from_prefab` | name | — | Listen to every entity made from this prefab, placed in the scene (whatever keys it overrides) or spawned later: `from_prefab = "coin"` instead of one [[connect]] per coin. |
| `signal` | name | **required** | Signal name, e.g. `pressed`, `released`, `tapped`, `changed`, `spawned`, `refused`. |
| `to` | name | — | Name of the target entity, or `self` for the entity that emitted (with `from_prefab`). Required for every action except `spawn`. |
| `action` | enable \| disable \| toggle \| add \| set \| spawn | — | enable, disable or toggle the target; `add` a number to / `set` one of its props; or `spawn` a new copy of `prefab` where the signal happened. Use exactly one of `action` and `actions`. |
| `prop` | name | — | With `add`/`set`: the target's prop (declared in its `props`). |
| `value` | bool \| number \| string | — | With `add`: the number to add (default 1; negative subtracts). With `set`: the new value (required), of the prop's type. |
| `prefab` | name | — | With `spawn`: the prefab to place. It goes on the tapped cell (`from = "ground"`) or the emitter's cell, with its `footprint` toward +x and +y, if every covered cell is inside the ground, on terrain with `build = true` and free: no enabled entity that is drawn there, solid, an actor or a trigger (data-only entities with just props take up no space). Otherwise nothing is placed (`blocked`, reason `edge`, `terrain` or `occupied`) and the source of the signal (the ground, for ground taps) emits `refused` on that cell, if a [[connect]] listens. |
| `cost` | table: cost | — | With `spawn`: the price, paid from a prop only if the copy is placed: `cost = { entity = "town", prop = "coins", amount = 3 }`. If the prop is below `amount`, nothing is placed or paid (`blocked`, reason `funds`, checked before the cell) and the signal's source emits `refused` with reason `funds`. |
| `when` | [{ condition }, ...] | — | Conditions that must all hold when the signal arrives, or the action is skipped (logged as `skipped`). They are checked once, before the first action. For OR, write one `[[connect]]` per alternative. Item keys: `rwgpu explain condition`. |
| `actions` | [{ action }, ...] | — | Several actions for the same signal and `when`, run in order: `actions = [{ action = "set", to = "town", prop = "tool", value = "tree" }, { action = "set", to = "hint", prop = "msg", value = "" }]`. Each item has the keys `action`, `to`, `prop`, `value`, `prefab` and `cost` (`rwgpu explain action`), which then cannot be on the [[connect]] itself. If a `spawn` in the list cannot be placed, the actions after it do not run. |

### `connect action`

One item of a `[[connect]]` `actions` list: the same keys as a single-action [[connect]]. Items run in order after the connection's `when` held (checked once, before the first). A `spawn` that cannot be placed stops the rest of the list (logged as `skipped`), so `[{ action = "spawn", prefab = "house" }, { action = "add", to = "town", prop = "coins", value = -3 }]` pays only for a house that was placed.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | enable \| disable \| toggle \| add \| set \| spawn | **required** | enable, disable or toggle the target; `add` a number to / `set` one of its props; or `spawn` a new copy of `prefab` where the signal happened. |
| `to` | name | — | Name of the target entity, or `self` for the entity that emitted (with `from_prefab`). Required for every action except `spawn`. |
| `prop` | name | — | With `add`/`set`: the target's prop (declared in its `props`). |
| `value` | bool \| number \| string | — | With `add`: the number to add (default 1; negative subtracts). With `set`: the new value (required), of the prop's type. |
| `prefab` | name | — | With `spawn`: the prefab to place. It goes on the tapped cell (`from = "ground"`) or the emitter's cell, with its `footprint` toward +x and +y, if every covered cell is inside the ground, on terrain with `build = true` and free: no enabled entity that is drawn there, solid, an actor or a trigger (data-only entities with just props take up no space). Otherwise nothing is placed (`blocked`, reason `edge`, `terrain` or `occupied`) and the source of the signal (the ground, for ground taps) emits `refused` on that cell, if a [[connect]] listens. |
| `cost` | table: cost | — | With `spawn`: the price, paid from a prop only if the copy is placed: `cost = { entity = "town", prop = "coins", amount = 3 }`. If the prop is below `amount`, nothing is placed or paid (`blocked`, reason `funds`, checked before the cell) and the signal's source emits `refused` with reason `funds`. |

### `when condition`

One item of a `[[connect]]` `when` list, checked against the current state when the signal arrives. Names an `entity` and exactly one of `occupied`, `enabled` or `prop`: `{ entity = "plate_b", occupied = true }`, `{ entity = "gate", enabled = false }`, `{ entity = "hud", prop = "coins", at_least = 3 }` (a `counts` prop counts copies: `{ entity = "job", prop = "houses", at_least = 2 }`). On `signal = "refused"` only, `{ reason = "terrain" }` (no entity) picks one reason.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | name | — | The entity to look at, by name. Required, except in a `reason` condition. |
| `occupied` | bool | — | true: an enabled actor or pushable is on the entity's cell right now (for a trigger: one its `only` accepts). false: nothing is. |
| `enabled` | bool | — | The entity's enabled state. |
| `prop` | name | — | One of the entity's props, compared with `equals`, `at_least` and/or `at_most`. |
| `equals` | bool \| number \| string | — | With `prop`: the prop has exactly this value. |
| `at_least` | number | — | With `prop`: the number prop is ≥ this. |
| `at_most` | number | — | With `prop`: the number prop is ≤ this. |
| `reason` | edge \| terrain \| occupied \| funds | — | Only with `signal = "refused"`, and alone: the spawn was refused for this reason (outside the ground, terrain with `build = false`, a taken cell, or too little to pay its `cost`). |


## Prefabs: prefabs/<name>.toml

`prefab = "wall"` starts an entity from prefabs/wall.toml; keys on the entity override the prefab's, and component tables merge key by key (`block = { color = "#f00" }` keeps the prefab's height).

### `prefab file`

A reusable entity template: prefabs/<name>.toml. Same keys as an entity, minus name/prefab/pos/cells.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | — | What the prefab is. |
| `footprint` | [x, y] int | `[1, 1]` | Cells covered [along x, along y], from `pos` toward +x and +y: `[2, 2]` at pos [3, 4] covers [3, 4], [4, 4], [3, 5] and [4, 5]. Blocks and tiles fill the whole area; a sprite or label stands at its middle. It blocks, counts for triggers and is tapped on every covered cell. Only things that stay put can be bigger than one cell (no mover, patrol, wander, pushable or screen_pos). |
| `enabled` | bool | `true` | Disabled entities are not drawn, not solid, cannot be tapped and run no behaviors. |
| `solid` | bool | `false` | Nothing can move into its cell. |
| `pushable` | bool | `false` | A crate or weight. A mover that walks into it pushes it one cell, if the cell beyond is inside the ground and free (nothing solid, no actor, no other pushable); otherwise the mover is refused (`blocked`, reason `push`). Patrols and wanderers cannot push it: it blocks them like a solid. It holds pressure plates: triggers count it like an actor (`only` can name it). It cannot have mover, patrol or wander. |
| `tile` | table: tile | — | Flat diamond on the floor (marks, pressure plates). |
| `block` | table: block | — | Isometric box (walls, crates, buildings). |
| `sprite` | table: sprite | — | Upright shape standing on the cell (characters, items). |
| `mover` | table: mover | — | Moves one cell per direction input. |
| `patrol` | table: patrol | — | Walks a fixed path of cells. |
| `wander` | table: wander | — | Walks randomly (seeded). |
| `trigger` | table: trigger | — | Emits signals when actors step on or off its cell. |
| `label` | table: label | — | Text drawn with the built-in pixel font (scores, names). |
| `screen_pos` | [x, y] | — | Draw this entity on the screen instead of in the world (a HUD): `[x, y]` is the top-left pixel of its sprite and label. Screen entities are drawn above the world, ignore the camera, can be tapped, and can only have `sprite` and `label`. |
| `props` | table | — | Game data: numbers, text and flags, e.g. `{ score = 0 }`. A prop's type is fixed by its starting value. `[[connect]]` `add`/`set` change props at runtime, `when` conditions and label `{placeholders}` read them, `inspect` shows them and `[[expect]] props` checks them. |
| `counts` | table: prop = "prefab" | — | Props that count enabled copies of a prefab, kept up to date by the engine: `counts = { houses = "house" }` makes `houses` an integer prop equal to the number of enabled `house` entities (placed in the scene or spawned; an entity with `prefab = "house"` is a copy whatever keys it overrides). It changes when a copy is spawned, disabled or enabled again; the entity then emits `changed`, so labels, `when` conditions and `[[expect]] props` read it like any prop. `add`/`set` cannot change it. |
| `allow` | ["W....", ...] | — | Warning codes that are intended for this entity and should not be reported, e.g. `["W0201"]` for deliberately stacked solids. Errors cannot be allowed. |
| `shape` | [[shape]] | — | What it is built of: solids with flat colors, one `[[shape]]` table each (in a scene: `[[entity.shape]]`, or `shape = [{ ... }]`). A list here replaces the prefab's. |


## Components

Tables an entity or prefab can carry. An empty table (`mover = {}`) adds the component with defaults. `shape` is a list of tables, one per solid.

### `tile`

A flat diamond drawn on the floor at the entity's cell, above the ground.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#c9b26b"` | Fill color. |

### `block`

An isometric box filling the entity's cell (or its whole `footprint`). Left and right faces are shaded automatically.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#9aa0a6"` | Wall color; the top face too unless `top` is given. |
| `top` | color | — | Top face color (a roof, the water in a well). Default: `color`. |
| `height` | number 0–64 | `1.0` | Height in z units. |

### `[[shape]]`

One solid of an entity's shape list: a `kind` that fills the box from `at` to `at + size`, in one flat color, shaded by the scene's light like a block. `at` is counted in cells from the entity's own corner (the lowest x and y of its footprint, at its height): `at = [0, 0, 1.5]`, `size = [2, 2, 0.8]` is a roof on a 2 x 2 house 1.5 high. Shapes are drawn in list order and stay inside the footprint (W0208). Two shapes must not have upright sides in one plane that overlap (W0209).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | box \| roof \| wedge \| cylinder \| cone | **required** | `box`; `roof`: a gable roof, its ridge along x; `wedge`: a ramp or lean-to roof that rises toward +x; `cylinder` and `cone`: round, upright. |
| `at` | [x, y, z?] | `[0, 0, 0]` | The corner of its box with the lowest x, y and z. |
| `size` | [x, y, z] | **required** | The size of its box along x, y and z, in cells. |
| `color` | color | `"#9aa0a6"` | Its color (no see-through colors). |
| `turn` | 0 \| 90 \| 180 \| 270 | `0` | Quarter turns of the solid inside its box, from +x toward +y: at 90 a roof's ridge runs along y and a wedge rises toward +y, at 180 toward -x. |

### `sprite`

An upright shape whose bottom edge stands on the middle of the entity's cell.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | circle \| rect \| diamond | `"circle"` | circle (ellipse filling size), rect or diamond. |
| `color` | color | `"#ffffff"` | Fill color. |
| `size` | [x, y] | `[24, 32]` | Width and height in pixels. |
| `offset` | [x, y] | `[0, 0]` | Shift in pixels [right, down] from the standing point. |

### `mover`

Moves one cell per `up`/`down`/`left`/`right` input: up = -y, down = +y, left = -x, right = +x. Every enabled mover responds to the same input. A press or hold moves on its first frame if the mover is ready, then every `step_frames` while held. Input during the wait is not queued: a press is dropped (logged as `blocked`, reason `cooldown`); a hold moves as soon as the wait ends. A refused move also starts the wait, so a held direction retries every `step_frames`. Solids, other actors and the ground's edge also block, each logged as a `blocked` event with its reason.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step_frames` | integer 1–600 | `8` | Frames from one move to the next. `hold` for `step_frames × N` frames gives exactly N steps. |

### `patrol`

Walks `path` one cell at a time (x first, then y), starting from its `pos` toward `path[0]` (or `path[1]` if it starts on `path[0]`). The k-th step attempt happens in step k × step_frames − 1, so it is visible from frame k × step_frames. A blocked attempt is retried at the next attempt time.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | [[x, y], ...] | **required** | Cells to visit, in order. |
| `step_frames` | integer 1–6000 | `30` | Frames between step attempts. |
| `mode` | loop \| pingpong | `"loop"` | loop: back to the first cell; pingpong: walk the path backwards. |

### `wander`

Every `step_frames` (attempt k in step k × step_frames − 1, like patrol), draws one number from the world's seeded RNG: stay, or try one step up/down/left/right. Runs with the same seed repeat exactly.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step_frames` | integer 1–6000 | `45` | Frames between steps. |
| `area` | [[x, y], ...] | — | Two corner cells [[x0, y0], [x1, y1]] to stay inside. Default: the whole ground. |

### `trigger`

Watches its own cell. Emits `on_enter` when the first actor (an entity with mover, patrol or wander) or pushable arrives and `on_exit` when the last one leaves.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on_enter` | name | `"pressed"` | Signal emitted when the cell becomes occupied. |
| `on_exit` | name | `"released"` | Signal emitted when the cell becomes empty. |
| `only` | name | — | Only this entity (by name) counts. Default: any actor. |

### `label`

Text drawn with rwgpu's built-in pixel font (printable ASCII; `\n` starts a new line). `{name}` is replaced by the entity's prop `name` every frame, so `text = "Coins: {coins}/3"` shows the current count; `{{` and `}}` print braces. Each character is 6 × `scale` pixels wide (5 + 1 space) and lines are 10 × `scale` pixels apart; the text box is (6 × characters − 1) × scale wide and (10 × lines − 2) × scale tall. In the world the box's bottom edge is centered on the entity's cell, like a sprite; with `screen_pos` its top-left corner is at `screen_pos`. `offset` shifts it either way.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | **required** | The text, with `{prop}` placeholders. |
| `color` | color | `"#ffffff"` | Text color. |
| `scale` | integer 1–8 | `1` | Pixel size of the font: 2 doubles it. |
| `offset` | [x, y] | `[0, 0]` | Shift in pixels [right, down]. |


## Playtests: tests/*.toml

Scripted input and checks, run by `rwgpu test`. Any playtest can also drive `run`, `shot` and `inspect` with `--input`.

### `playtest file`

Scripted input plus expectations, run by `rwgpu test`. `run`, `shot` and `inspect` accept it as `--input`.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test` | table: playtest.test | — | Which scene, how long, which seed. |
| `input` | [[input]] | — | Scripted input, one `[[input]]` per event. |
| `expect` | [[expect]] | — | Checks on world state or the event log. |
| `shot` | [[shot]] | — | Screenshots compared with reference images. |

### `[test]`

Playtest settings.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | string | — | What the playtest checks. |
| `scene` | path | — | Scene to run. Default: the project's main_scene. |
| `frames` | integer ≥ 1 | `300` | Number of frames (steps) to run. |
| `seed` | integer ≥ 0 | — | Overrides the project and scene seed. |

### `[[input]]`

One input event. Use exactly one of `press`, `hold`, `tap` or `camera`. Input at frame N is applied by step N (the step from frame N to N+1). A `camera` move at frame N happens before that frame's taps.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | integer ≥ 0 | **required** | Frame at which the input happens. |
| `press` | up \| down \| left \| right \| confirm \| cancel | — | Press and release an action within the frame. |
| `hold` | up \| down \| left \| right \| confirm \| cancel | — | Hold an action down for `for` frames. |
| `for` | integer ≥ 1 | `1` | With `hold`: number of frames to hold. |
| `tap` | [x, y] | — | Tap the screen at pixel [x, y]; hits the topmost enabled entity drawn there. |
| `camera` | table: playtest.input.camera | — | Move the camera: `{ turn = 90 }`, `{ zoom = 2 }`, `{ pan = [1, 0] }`, `{ view = "perspective" }`, or several at once. What a later tap hits depends on it. |

### `camera`

One move of the camera, as a player would make it. The parts given are applied together.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | iso \| perspective | — | Switch to this view (`iso` or `perspective`). |
| `turn` | number -360–360 | `0` | Turn by this many degrees about the vertical line through the camera's center. |
| `zoom` | number 0.1–10 | `1.0` | Multiply the zoom by this (it stays within 0.125–16). |
| `pan` | [x, y] | `[0, 0]` | Move the camera's center by this many cells [x, y]. It stops at the edge of the ground's cells (with no ground, of what the world holds at the start): `rwgpu inspect` shows where, as the camera's `bound`. |

### `[[expect]]`

A check at `frame`. Entity state (`entity` with `pos`/`enabled`/`solid`/`props`/`text`), a count of entities made from a prefab (`prefab` with `count`, optionally at `pos`), or the event log (`event`, filtered by `entity`, `other`, `signal`, `reason`, counted with `at_least`/`at_most`). Events are counted if they happened *before* `frame`: an event logged as `[N]` happened in step N and counts from `frame = N + 1`. `entity` matches the event's subject and `other` its other party (`rwgpu explain events` lists both for every kind).

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | integer ≥ 0 | — | When to check. Default: the last frame. |
| `entity` | name | — | Entity to check, by name. |
| `pos` | [x, y, z?] | — | Expected position. |
| `enabled` | bool | — | Expected enabled state. |
| `solid` | bool | — | Expected solid state. |
| `props` | table | — | Expected values of these props (others are ignored). |
| `text` | string | — | Expected label text as shown, with placeholders filled in (`"Coins: 3/3"`). |
| `prefab` | name | — | Without `event`: count the enabled entities made from this prefab (placed or spawned), optionally only those at `pos`, checked with `count` (at least one when absent). With `event`: only count events about the prefab: its spawns, refused spawns (`blocked`) and skipped spawns, and events whose subject is a copy of it (`event = "skipped", prefab = "barn"` = barn spawns stopped by a `when`). |
| `count` | integer ≥ 0 | — | With `prefab`: exactly this many. `count = 0` with `pos` asserts nothing of that prefab stands there. |
| `event` | input \| tap \| tap_miss \| moved \| blocked \| trigger \| signal \| action \| skipped \| spawned \| counted \| error \| custom \| omitted | — | Count events of this kind that happened before `frame`. |
| `other` | name | — | With `event`: only events whose other party is this entity (the blocker of `blocked`, the actor of `trigger`, the emitter of `action`). |
| `signal` | name | — | With `event`: only count events about this signal. |
| `reason` | solid \| actor \| edge \| area \| cooldown \| push \| terrain \| occupied \| funds | — | With `event = "blocked"`: only count refusals for this reason (e.g. `solid`, not `cooldown`; `push` = a pushable could not be pushed; `terrain`/`occupied`/`edge` = a spawn could not be placed; `funds` = it could not be paid for). |
| `changed` | bool | — | With `event = "action"`: `true` counts only actions that really changed something (a door that opened, a prop with a new value), `false` only those that changed nothing (`enable` on an enabled entity, `set` to the same value). Without it, every time the connection fired counts. |
| `at_least` | integer ≥ 0 | `1` | With `event`: minimum number of matching events (0 when only `at_most` is given). |
| `at_most` | integer ≥ 0 | — | With `event`: maximum number of matching events. `at_most = 0` asserts it never happened. |

### `[[shot]]`

Render a frame and compare it with a reference PNG. Create or refresh references with `rwgpu test --update-refs`.

| key | type | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | integer ≥ 0 | — | Frame to render. Default: the last frame. |
| `reference` | path | **required** | Reference PNG, relative to the project root (e.g. tests/refs/smoke.png). |
| `max_diff_pixels` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Pixels allowed to differ. |


## Runtime rules

**Frames.** The simulation advances in fixed steps (`[sim] tick_rate` per second). Frame N is the state
after N steps. An `[[input]]` at frame N is applied by step N. `run --frames 300` takes 300 steps;
`shot --frame 300` and `inspect --frame 300` show the state after them. Everything is deterministic: same
files + input + seed = same state hash and same pixels, on every machine. A state hash fingerprints the
state at one frame (what `rwgpu test` prints is the final frame's), not the path that led there: two runs
can differ along the way and still end in the same state.

**Coordinates.** Cells are `[x, y]` integers; `[0, 0]` is the top corner of the ground. z is height.
Direction inputs move movers: `up` = -y, `down` = +y, `left` = -x, `right` = +x. With the camera a scene
starts with by default (`view = "iso"`, no `turn`, `zoom = 1`), +x runs down-right on screen and +y
down-left, and grid point (x, y, z) is drawn at this pixel from the top-left:
`sx = ox + (x - y) × tile_width / 2`, `sy = oy + (x + y) × tile_height / 2 - z × z_height`, where (ox, oy) is
chosen so the camera `center` (default: the middle of the ground) lands in the middle of the frame. A sprite's
bottom edge sits at its cell's (sx, sy); `offset` shifts it.

**The camera.** The world is 3D and the camera is part of the game's state. `[camera]` in the scene sets
where it starts (`center`, `turn`, `zoom`, `view = "iso"` or `"perspective"`); `[[input]] camera = { turn =
90 }` (also `zoom`, `pan`, `view`) moves it during a playtest, as a player would. Once it has moved, the
formula above no longer holds: ask the engine. `rwgpu inspect --frame N --json` gives each entity's `screen`
rectangle and a `tap` pixel under the camera of that frame, `--place house@3,4` gives the pixel that taps
that ground cell, and the top-level `camera` field says where the camera is. A camera move at frame N
happens before the taps of frame N. The camera is not part of the state hash (it is not in the world); a
picture taken after a move is.

**Step order.** Each step: input (taps resolve to the topmost enabled entity drawn under the point and
emit `tapped`; a tap that hits no entity but lands on a ground cell makes the ground emit `tapped`, if a
`[[connect]] from = "ground"` listens), movers, patrols, wanderers, Rust game systems, triggers, then signal
dispatch through `[[connect]]` tables.

**Limits.** A project over a limit checked at `load` is refused where it goes over (E0209), before the work
it would cause, and nothing after that point in the file is read. A step that reaches one of the others
stops there: the signals still queued are dropped, an `error` event says what was cut off, and `rwgpu run`,
`inspect`, `shot` and `test` report the code as an error. Every other step runs as before. The ranges of
single values are in the tables above.

| limit | number | checked | code | what happens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bytes in a file | 67108864 | load | E0209 | Bytes in one file of a project (64 MiB). A larger file is not read. |
| entities in a scene | 1000000 | load | E0209 | Entities in one scene; each cell of a `cells` list is one. The scene is read up to the [[entity]] table that goes over. |
| cells of a ground | 16777216 | load | E0209 | Cells of a ground, `size` x by y or the map's (4096 x 4096). A larger ground is not made. |
| cells covered in a scene | 4194304 | load | E0209 | Cells the entities of one scene cover, each `footprint` counted in full (2048 x 2048). The scene is read up to the [[entity]] table that goes over. |
| prefab bytes copied in a scene | 134217728 | load | E0209 | Bytes of prefab files copied into the entities of one scene: each prefab's size, once for every entity made from it (128 MiB). The scene is read up to the [[entity]] table that goes over. |
| characters in a name | 128 | load | E0209 | Characters in a name or in a key. A file with a longer one is not read past its schema check. |
| tables in a playtest | 100000 | load | E0209 | `[[input]]`, `[[expect]]` and `[[shot]]` tables in one playtest. A longer playtest is not run. |
| shapes in a list | 64 | load | E0209 | `[[shape]]` tables in one list, a prefab's or an entity's. A file with a longer list is not read past its schema check. |
| signals per step | 1000 | step | E0301 | Signals dispatched in one step. The rest of the step's signals are dropped: usually a loop of connections. |
| actions per step | 10000 | step | E0302 | `[[connect]]` actions run or skipped in one step. The step stops at the next one and drops the signals still queued: one signal can reach many connections with many actions each. |
| count changes per step | 10000 | step | E0303 | `counts` props changed in one step. The step stops there and drops the signals still queued; the next step brings the remaining counts up to date. |
| entities in a world | 1000000 | step | E0304 | Entities a world may hold, spawned ones included (no entity is ever removed). A spawn beyond it is not placed; the step stops there and drops the signals still queued. |
| taps per step | 256 | step | E0305 | Taps applied in one step, from a playtest or a player. The first ones are applied in order; the rest are not looked at. |
| events of one kind per step | 256 | events | — | `moved`, `blocked` (for a move), `trigger` and `custom` events written in one step, per kind. The rest are counted, one `omitted` event per kind says how many, and the entities a run watches (`--watch NAME`) have all of theirs written. Every other kind is bounded by the step's limits and always written. |
| events kept | 100000 | events | — | Events the log keeps. When it is full, the oldest half is dropped and counted (`events_dropped`); ask for an earlier frame (`--frame`, `--since`) to see them. |


**Actors and blocking.** Entities with `mover`, `patrol` or `wander` are actors. A move is refused when
the target cell is outside the ground, holds an enabled `solid` entity, or holds another enabled actor.
A `pushable` entity blocks like a solid, except that a mover walking into it pushes it one cell (its
`moved` event, cause `pushed`, comes just before the mover's): the cell beyond must be inside the ground
and free of solids, actors and other pushables, or the mover is refused with reason `push`. Patrols and
wanderers never push.

**Ground and terrain.** `[ground] size = [w, h]` is plain ground. `[ground] map` is one string per row
(y = 0 first), one character per cell (x = 0 first); every character is declared by a `[[terrain]]` table
with a `name`, colors and `build` (whether spawned things may be placed on it). `rwgpu inspect --json`
shows the map and legend under `ground`.

**Footprints.** `footprint = [w, h]` makes an entity cover w × h cells from its `pos` toward +x and +y (its
`pos` is the back corner, nearest the top of the screen). It blocks, counts for triggers, takes up space
for placement and is tapped on every covered cell. A block or tile fills the whole area; a sprite or label
stands at the middle and is drawn with the front cell. Only things that stay put can be bigger than one
cell.

**Spawning.** `action = "spawn"` with `prefab` places a new copy of the prefab where the signal happened: on
the tapped cell for `from = "ground"`, else on the emitter's cell (its back corner there). Every covered cell
must be inside the ground, on terrain with `build = true` and free: no enabled entity that is drawn there,
solid, an actor or a trigger (data-only entities with just props take no space). A spawn with
`cost = { entity = "town", prop = "coins", amount = 3 }` also needs that prop to be at least `amount` (checked
first, before the cell) and pays it only when the copy is placed. Otherwise nothing is placed or paid and a
`blocked` event (`cause = "spawn"`, reason `funds`, `edge`, `terrain` or `occupied`) says why; then the source
of the signal (the ground, for ground taps; else the emitter) emits `refused` on that cell if a connection
listens, and `when = [{ reason = "terrain" }]` picks one reason. A spawn stopped by its own `when` is
`skipped`, not refused, and emits nothing.
A new copy gets the next id (`#12 (house)`), has no name, and emits `spawned` if a connection listens.
`from_prefab = "house"` listens to every copy of a prefab, placed or spawned, and `to = "self"` targets the
copy that emitted. `rwgpu inspect --place house@3,4` answers "can I build here?" at any frame (with a pixel
that taps that ground cell); `--place house` lists every cell where it fits.

**Enabled.** Disabled entities are not drawn, not solid, cannot be tapped, run no behaviors and do not
count for triggers. `[[connect]]` actions `enable`, `disable` and `toggle` change this. Enabling a solid
entity where an actor stands does not push the actor out.

**Input.** Every enabled `mover` responds to the same input. Actors and pushables set off triggers.

**Signals.** Every entity emits `tapped` when tapped. A `trigger` emits `on_enter` (default `pressed`)
when its cell goes from empty to occupied by an enabled actor and `on_exit` (default `released`) when it
empties. Occupancy is re-checked every step, so enabling or disabling an actor that stands on the cell
counts too (the signal comes in the next step's trigger phase). A trigger that is already occupied at
frame 0 does **not** emit: start the connected door in the state you want (e.g. `enabled = false`), or use
a `when` condition, which looks at the current state rather than at signals.

**Props and conditions.** `[[connect]]` `add` and `set` change a prop of `to` (a prop's type is fixed by its
declared starting value). When the value really changes and some `[[connect]]` listens to `changed` from that
entity, it emits `changed`. Signals are dispatched first in, first out, each to its connections in file order,
within the same step. `when` conditions are checked as the signal is dispatched, against the state at that
moment (this step's positions and occupancy, plus the actions already applied in this step); if one fails,
nothing is done and a `skipped` event names the condition and what was seen.

**Several actions.** `actions = [{ action = "set", to = "town", ... }, { ... }]` runs several actions for
one signal, in order, as one `[[connect]]`: its `when` is checked once, before the first, so an earlier
action cannot make a later one skip. If a `spawn` in the list cannot be placed, the actions after it do not
run (each logs `skipped`, `stopped_by = "refused spawn"`), so `[spawn, pay]` pays only for what was placed.
Every action logs its own `action` (or `skipped`) event, as separate connections would.

**Counts.** `counts = { houses = "house" }` gives an entity an integer prop `houses` that the engine keeps
equal to the number of enabled `house` entities (placed in the scene or spawned). It is updated in the same
step as the spawn, `disable`, `enable` or `toggle` that changes it, logged as a `counted` event, and its
owner then emits `changed` (if a connection listens), so labels, `when` and `[[expect]] props` read it like
any prop. `add`/`set` cannot change it.

**Events.** Every step logs what happened and what was refused, with a sentence and structured fields.
Read them with `rwgpu inspect --events` or `rwgpu run --events`; `rwgpu explain events` prints this table.
In a step with more than 256 `moved` events (or `blocked` events of moves, `trigger` or `custom` events),
the first 256 of that kind are written and the others counted: an `omitted` event at the end of the step
says how many, and `event_counts` counts every event that happened, written or not (`events_omitted` the
ones not written). Watching writes everything about an entity whatever the count: `--watch NAME` on
`rwgpu run` and `rwgpu inspect`, `inspect --entity NAME --events`, and a playtest for the entities its
`[[expect]]` tables name. A replay is deterministic, so running again with a watch gives the detail of any
step. Other kinds are always written: the limits above bound them.

Every event has `frame` (the step that produced it: `[N]` happened in step N, so it is part of the state from frame N + 1), `kind`, `entity` (the subject), `other` (if any) and `message`.

| kind | `entity` (subject) | `other` | extra fields | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `input` | — | — | pressed | Actions that went down this step. |
| `tap` | the entity hit (none for a ground tap) | — | x, y, signal; cell (ground taps) | A tap hit the topmost enabled entity under the point; it emits `tapped`. A tap that hits no entity but lands on a ground cell is a ground tap when a [[connect]] listens to `from = "ground"`: the ground emits `tapped` with that `cell`. |
| `tap_miss` | topmost disabled entity under the point, if any | — | x, y, under_disabled; cell (when over the ground) | A tap hit nothing enabled (and, over the ground, nothing listens to the ground's `tapped`). |
| `moved` | the entity that moved | the pusher (when `cause` is `pushed`) | cause, from, to, by | One cell of movement. `cause` is the direction, `patrol`, `wander` or `pushed` (a pushable moved by a mover; logged just before the mover's own move). |
| `blocked` | the mover (none for a spawn) | the blocker (for `solid` and `actor`), the pushable that would not move (for `push`), the entity in the way (for `occupied`), the payer (for `funds`) | cause, from, to, reason, frames_left; beyond, push_blocked, push_blocked_by (for `push`); prefab, at, cell, terrain, cost (for a spawn) | A move or a placement was refused. For moves, `reason`: solid, actor, edge, area, cooldown, or push (the pushable in the way could not move: `push_blocked` says why). For a `spawn` (`cause = "spawn"`): funds (the payer of its `cost` has too little; checked first, `other` = the payer, `cost` = what it needed), edge (a cell outside the ground), terrain (a cell whose terrain has `build = false`) or occupied (an enabled entity covers a cell); `cell` is the cell that failed. When a [[connect]] listens, the source of the spawn's signal (the ground, for ground taps) then emits `refused` on `at` (`signal = "refused"` here). |
| `trigger` | the trigger | the actor that entered or left | signal, by | The trigger's cell became occupied or empty; it emits `signal`. |
| `signal` | the emitter | — | signal, connections; reason (for `refused`) | A signal was dispatched to this many `[[connect]]` tables (0 = nothing listens). A `refused` signal carries the spawn's `reason` (edge, terrain or occupied), which `when = [{ reason = ... }]` tests. |
| `action` | the target | the emitter | signal, action, before, after, changed; prop, value (add/set); when (each condition, held, seen) | A connection's action ran on its target: enable, disable, toggle, or add/set a prop (`before`/`after` are the enabled state or the prop's values). It is logged even when nothing changes (`enable` on an enabled entity: "stays enabled", `changed = false`), so `[[expect]] event = "action"` counts every time the connection fired; add `changed = true` to count only real changes. |
| `skipped` | the target (none for `spawn`) | the emitter | signal, action, prop, prefab, cell, when (each condition, held, seen); stopped_by | A connection's signal arrived, but a `when` condition did not hold, so nothing was done. The message names the first failing condition and what was seen. One event per action of an `actions` list; an action after a `spawn` that could not be placed is skipped too (`stopped_by = "refused spawn"`). |
| `spawned` | the new entity | the emitter of the signal (none for a ground tap) | prefab, cell, cells; paid (entity, prop, amount, before, after) with a `cost` | A `spawn` action placed a new copy of `prefab` with its back corner on `cell`, covering `cells`. It gets the next free id (`#N (prefab)` in messages) and emits `spawned` if a [[connect]] listens (`from_prefab`). |
| `counted` | the entity whose `counts` prop changed | — | prop, prefab, before, after | A `counts` prop now has a new number of enabled `prefab` copies, because a copy was spawned, disabled or enabled. The message says which; the entity then emits `changed` if a [[connect]] listens (once when several of its counts change together). |
| `error` | the emitter | — | code, signal | A step reached one of the engine's limits and stopped there: more than 1000 signals (E0301) or 10000 actions (E0302) in one step, 10000 count changes (E0303), a spawn beyond 1000000 entities (E0304), more than 256 taps (E0305); or a spawn of a prefab the world does not have (E0201). The message says what was cut off; `rwgpu run` reports the code as a diagnostic. |
| `custom` | set by game code | set by game code | set by game code | Logged by Rust game code. |
| `omitted` | — | — | of, count, written | More than 256 `moved`, `blocked` (for a move), `trigger` or `custom` events happened in one step: the first 256 of that kind (`of`) were written and `count` more were counted, not written. Logged at the end of the step, once per kind. The entities a run watches (`--watch NAME` on `rwgpu run` and `rwgpu inspect`, or `inspect --entity NAME --events`) have all of their events written. |


**Drawing.** The world is drawn in 3D: what is nearer the camera hides what is behind it, whatever the
order in the file. A block is a box; a tile and a ground cell are flat. A flat thing lying exactly on a
surface shows on top of it: a tile on the ground or on a block's top, a block of height 0 on a tile. A
sprite or a label is a flat picture that faces the camera and stands on its entity's standing point (on
top of its block, if it has one): a sprite grows and shrinks with the camera like the world, text keeps its
pixel size. See-through colors blend over what is behind them. Screen entities (`screen_pos`) are drawn
after the whole world, in file order, and ignore the camera.
One fixed light shades boxes: a top keeps its color, and the sides get 0.8 (+y), 0.65 (+x), 0.5 (-x) and
0.35 (-y) of theirs, so turning the camera shows the darker sides.
